messages:
anna: Heads-up: PR #5124 (microbatch allocator tweak) shows a memory uplift on long-seq workloads in my local stress runs. Putting this in perf-review — need 1x perf + 1x code approval before we merge.

anna: Short summary: +5% p90 latency, +8% resident memory on the nc-longseq benchmark. Roughly +120MB/GPU at 2k token seqs. Link: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/5124 :eyes:

kyle: Can you paste the exact bench command and the raw numbers? also pinging @lee for allocator context.

anna: bench command I ran:
```
./bench/run.sh --profile nc-longseq --batch 1 --microbatch 4 --iters 500 --seq 2048
```
Raw summary (median over 3 runs):
- baseline: p50 58ms, p90 120ms, mem 1480MB
- PR5124:   p50 61ms, p90 126ms, mem 1600MB
(throughput roughly same, memcpy counts increased)

bench-bot: Auto-run queued: ran PR5124 vs main on nc-longseq. Results uploaded to /bench/results/1776123456. Run IDs: r-8712 (main), r-8713 (PR5124). See diff: mem +8.1%, p90 +5.0%.

lee: Interesting. PR changes microbatch allocator to reuse a slightly larger slab to avoid fragmentation. That reduces alloc churn but increases peak resident when multiple long sequences run concurrently. Might be an expected tradeoff.

sara: Could we try same run with `--microbatch 2` and `--batch 2` to see if behavior shifts? If it's slab-size related the pattern will change.

anna: Re-ran with microbatch=2/batch=2:
```
- baseline: mem 1490MB, p90 118ms
- PR5124:   mem 1528MB, p90 119ms
```
So uplift reduced to ~+2.5% mem and p90 impact negligible.

kyle: That suggests microbatch sizing amplifies the effect. Can you also share pprof heap diff or top allocated objects?

anna: Pprof heap top diff:
```
+  48MB  allocs: buffer_slab::reuse
+  32MB  allocs: attention_kv_cache
+  20MB  other buffers
```
Slab reuse is the main delta.

lee: I think safe mitigation: 1) reduce default slab size for long-seq config; 2) add dynamic shrink after idle period. Both are small changes but need tests.

kyle: From perf POV: microbatch=4 default is common in hosted workloads. A +8% mem could push some Dedicated boxes over OOM margin. Need to be conservative.

sara: My vote: hold on merging until we either (A) add a config toggle to use old allocator for longseq profiles, or (B) make slab adaptive. Either needs a small follow-up PR but we can merge the fix instead of reverting.

anna: I can implement (A) quickly: restore previous slab thresholds under a `longseq_compat` flag defaulted to true for nc-longseq profile. Will add tests + perf doc. ETA EOD tomorrow.

repo-bot: PR 5124 is currently blocked: required-reviewers missing (eng-runtime). CI: all checks passed except nightly-memory (warn).

kyle: Sounds good. I'll hold the code approval until the toggle is in or until we have a clear canary plan. If you push the flag impl, ping me — I'll run a quick canary on dedicated-qa.

lee: +1 to canary gating. Also add a small smoke that runs longseq with microbatch=4 at PR-level to catch regressions earlier.

anna: Will add the toggle + smoke test. Also adding a short note in the PR about expected tradeoffs and bench artifacts.

kyle: ack. Once the toggle is in and canary looks clean, I can approve and we can merge with a short-lived feature-flag on. :thumbsup:

sara: Thanks for the thorough benching, anna. Appreciate the quick follow-up plan.

anna: Thanks all — working on the flag now, will post updated run IDs when ready.

repo-bot: Note: merging will auto-create a canary deploy if labelled `canary/auto`.
